messages.text:
I have a NerdOctAxe that has died. So I took the Lilgo off which I am sure is the same version, put Harlo OS on it and set ot up on the BC04. I have 5.5TH and all has been running for a few hours now getting shares fine.

Andrew T.

Hi Andrew,

That is excellent news, and it is a genuinely neat fix. The display on the NerdOctaxe is the same LilyGo T-Display S3 family that the BC04 expects, so swapping it in sidesteps the exact problem JD ran into: the screen that shipped on your BC04 is locked down by Hammer and will not take a Harlo OS flash. Yours now has an unlocked one, so the firmware wrote and booted normally. Five and a half TH with shares landing steadily for a few hours is a healthy BC04, so the module, the hashboard and the pool side are all doing what they should.

A couple of things worth knowing now that it is running. The hashrate on the unit's own screen is a short rolling average and will swing either side of 5.5 TH by a fair margin, while your pool figure will look lower for the first day or so and then settle close to the local number once it has enough shares to average over; that difference is normal and not a fault. Keep an eye on the chip temperature in the web UI for the first day, and if it climbs it is almost always airflow or room temperature rather than the board. Also check in the UI that you are on the current Harlo OS release, since the download page at harlolabs.com lists the latest version and the release notes, and update if you are behind.

On the NerdOctaxe itself, if you would like, tell me what it does now when you power it on, with the screen gone: any LEDs, fan movement, whether the web UI answers on your network. I will work through it with you the same way, because a dead screen and a dead board are very different problems and it is worth knowing which one you have before you write it off.

Glad it is hashing, and nice bit of work getting there.

Hal, HeliumDeploy technical support
